title: The local ring of a scheme-theoretic fibre is a quotient of the local ring
statement: Let $g:Y\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $y\in Y$ and $t=g(y)$, let $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ be the local rings (structure-sheaf stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]), $\mathfrak m_t$ the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{T,t}$, $\kappa(t)=\mathcal O_{T,t}/\mathfrak m_t$ [def-weil-residue-field], and $g^\sharp_y:\mathcal O_{T,t}\to\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ the stalk map of $g$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism]. Let $Y_t=Y\times_T\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(t)$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre with first projection $p:Y_t\to Y$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and let $y'\in Y_t$ be the unique point with $p(y')=y$. Then the stalk map $p^\sharp_{y'}:\mathcal O_{Y,y}\to\mathcal O_{Y_t,y'}$ is surjective and its kernel is the ideal $\mathfrak m_t\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ of $\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ generated by $g^\sharp_y(\mathfrak m_t)$. Hence $p^\sharp_{y'}$ induces a ring isomorphism $\mathcal O_{Y,y}/\mathfrak m_t\mathcal O_{Y,y}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_{Y_t,y'}$ sending the class of each element $z$ to $p^\sharp_{y'}(z)$.
